requirements.evidence: Contract fully matched: enum CallMode with the three backed values (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:18). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB inside the transaction (CallNextTicket.php:23-30); ordering priority DESC, issued_at, id (:132) and oldest-first for normals (:130); fairness only in Any mode using last 3 by called_at DESC, id DESC (:51, :101-110) and only when a normal waits (:52-56); per-candidate lockForUpdate + waiting re-check with skip (:64-76); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set and refreshed model returned (:78-83); dedicated exception when nothing eligible (:86). Small gaps: the 'normal waiting' check happens before candidate locking, so if every normal is concurrently called via Ticket::call() the action throws instead of falling back to priority tickets; the history query filters on status = called (:100) rather than on having been called (called_at), which may miscount if called tickets later move to another status.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions as a single use-case class; no service/repository layers; reuses InactiveQueueException; CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased] (CHANGELOG.md:9); docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md 'Call the next ticket' updated as required. Deviations: the existing TODO 'link the test covering the single-call invariant and concurrent-call protection once implemented' is left in place right after the new text claiming implementation (docs/architecture.md:209-210); the business-rules 'Single-ticket call' note documenting Ticket::call() was replaced rather than kept (docs/business-rules.md:228-229); the public __invoke has no PHPDoc while the private helpers do.

security.evidence: Authorization is explicitly out of scope (caller trusted) and documented as such (docs/architecture.md:202-203). No user input, no mass assignment (attributes set individually, CallNextTicket.php:78-81), stale model not trusted for is_active (:40-47), row locks prevent double calls (:65-68). No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers priority ordering, issued_at/id tie-breaks (:297-312), queue scoping and no re-call (:314-330), both restricted modes and their empty cases (:332-372), empty queue (:374), fairness trigger, reset, history from other modes, ignored in restricted modes, no-normal-waiting, fewer-than-3 (:381-456), inactive and stale-inactive queue (:458-480), and the returned-model contract (:482-499). Missing: no test of the skip-on-concurrently-called candidate path (CallNextTicket.php:74-76), and no test for the history tie-break by id when called_at is equal.

simplicity.evidence: Lean action with two small private helpers and no speculative abstraction. Minor redundancy: the condition `$mode === CallMode::NormalOnly || $restrictToNormal` is evaluated twice in orderedCandidateIds (CallNextTicket.php:124 and :128); the separate `$ticket === null` and status checks (:70-76) could be one condition.

readability.evidence: Clear names (priorityStreakReached, orderedCandidateIds, restrictToNormal), focused comments explaining the locking rationale (CallNextTicket.php:38-39, :61-63), typed closures and return types; tests use small helpers (waitingTicket, calledTicket) with descriptive it() names. No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Diff contains only the action, enum, exception, its tests, the two required docs and the CHANGELOG entry; no HTTP, Livewire, authorization or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The fairness restriction is decided with an unlocked exists() check; if the waiting normals are concurrently called via Ticket::call() before their row locks, every candidate is skipped and NoWaitingTicketsException is thrown although priority tickets are still waiting, contrary to 'if no normal is waiting, priority tickets keep being called'.
The exactly-once skip path (candidate locked and found no longer waiting, CallNextTicket.php:74-76) has no test, even though the task's rule 7 specifically calls for it.
The pre-existing TODO about linking the concurrent-call protection test is left unchanged right after new text describing that protection as implemented, so the docs contradict themselves.
Fairness history filters on status = called rather than on called_at being set, so tickets that move past 'called' in a future status would drop out of the streak history.
The note documenting the existing Ticket::call() single-ticket primitive was deleted instead of kept next to the new call-next description.
The NormalOnly/restrictToNormal condition is duplicated across the filter and ordering branches; one branch could apply both.
The public __invoke has no PHPDoc describing its thrown exceptions, while the conventions ask for PHPDoc on public methods touched.

review.summary: The change adds CallNextTicket with the CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, matching the contract exactly. It locks the queue row and re-reads is_active, orders candidates deterministically, applies the 3-call fairness rule only in Any mode, and locks and re-checks each candidate; it also ships thorough Pest tests and the required doc and CHANGELOG updates. I'd approve it with nits: a narrow concurrency edge case in the fairness fallback, no test for the skip-on-concurrent-call path, and a stale TODO left in the architecture docs.
